issue.title: Deploy guard wedges the vault when a rebased landing leaves no byte-identical commit
issue.description: ## Bug - **Location:** src/native/plugins/deploy.rs evaluate_guard Problem: evaluate_guard in src/native/plugins/deploy.rs accepts another checkout's dirty deploy only through a byte-identical commit. A phase that rebases over parallel work never produces one, so the guard refuses and agents leave the vault stale. Observed 2026-11-17: bob-cli_15 dirty b0a9c89 deploy of bob-ledger-tools (v1.129.0) refused every later sync even after ms.3 landed as rebased 60b5602 (ancestor of master f80d0dd); ms.4, mu.1, mu.2 each recorded the refusal; vault stayed stale until this plan's authorized -F. Same wedge as bob-cli-lm note #2 (lj.4). Direction for planner: treat a stamped checkout that is now clean, whose HEAD is an ancestor of the incoming HEAD and has moved past source_head, as landed. Print the proving checkout, rely on sync backups, and keep refusing truly unlanded work. Size large: changes deploy-safety semantics and needs a design pass.

task_type_fields.impact: Every remaining phase of both epics hits the refusal; agents leave the vault stale with landed work not live; only hand-proved -F clears it.
task_type_fields.repro: 1. Dirty deploy from checkout A stamps source_head b0a9c89. 2. Land rebased commit 60b5602 on master. 3. From clean updated checkout run bob plugins sync --repo PWD --no-pull --dry-run -p bob-ledger-tools: refuses, no single commit holds the stamped bundle byte for byte.

issue.creation_reason: The co-landing plan hit the same dirty-deploy refusal across two epics after rebased landings, and the guard still requires a byte-identical commit that a rebase can never produce.
